## `std::time::Instant` vs `std::time::Duration`

- **`Instant`** is an opaque point-in-time measurement from a *monotonically nondecreasing clock*. It represents "when" something happened and is useful for measuring elapsed time (e.g., benchmarking, timeouts). It cannot be converted to a wall-clock timestamp and is only meaningful relative to other instants from the same clock. [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html)

- **`Duration`** is a *span of time* — a quantity, not a point. It represents "how long" something took, composed of whole seconds plus subsecond (nanosecond) precision. It is used to express intervals, such as system timeouts or elapsed-time results from `Instant::elapsed()`. [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Duration.html)

- **Relationship:** An `Instant` measures *when*; a `Duration` measures *how long*. Subtracting one `Instant` from another yields a `Duration` (e.g., `instant.elapsed()`), making `Duration` the bridge between two points on the monotonic clock.
